competency_fulfillment.rationale: Competency: "Collect data from experiments with a small number of possible outcomes (e.g., rolling a die or tossing a coin)." None of the five samples involve an actual chance experiment, die, or coin; they ask students to read pictograph/bar-graph values or fill in given totals instead.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: This node registers pictographs (2 axes/24 combos) and bar_graphs (3 axes/30 combos), a large combined space, but every sample shown draws from graph-reading/building content rather than an experiment-outcome-collection variant.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Question stems such as "Look at the picture graph. Each apple = 2. How many are in dogs?" run about 12-13 words, within the 22-word cap and readable for G3 Q3.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: pictographs and bar_graphs are presentation/interpretation DNAs, not experiment-simulation DNAs, so even a large 54-combo registry doesn't obviously support the small-number-of-outcomes experiment skill named here.

competency_alignment.rationale: This node's competency, data collection from chance experiments, is foundational and distinct from the graph-reading skills belonging to q3_1/q3_2; using graph-reading content skips the experiment step.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Values like 15/15/15/5 and pictograph counts scaled by 2 per icon are reasonable magnitudes for G3 graph work generally, but don't reflect the small 2-6 outcome scale a die/coin experiment would produce.
